target.location_description: outer continental shelf off Cochin/Kochi, Arabian Sea, approximately 65 km SW of Cochin in the 2016 source
target.official_cruise_program: Sea bed mapping, morphometry, sediment composition and sediment transport in the continental slope, off Cochin, Kerala

observed_target_evidence.claim: SR-004 high-resolution seabed survey detected an isolated large circular depression using swath bathymetry and sub-bottom profiling.
The depression is about 600 m in diameter and about 40 m maximum relief/depth; local shelf depths are about 155-160 m.
Regional seafloor is gently sloping at about 0.8 degrees; depression wall slopes reported around 7-20 degrees.
Sub-bottom profile shows sharply truncated sedimentary layers and a truncated-cone-like cross section.
A positive magnetic anomaly is reported over the depression and continues toward deeper water along all three profiles.
Free-air gravity was reported not to show the expected bathymetric low over the depression.
A 12.5 m core from the center did not yield minerals indicating shock metamorphism in the studied coarse fraction.
observed_target_evidence.constraint: Authors note the core may not have penetrated below younger crater-fill sediment, so this does not by itself falsify impact.

observed_target_evidence.claim: An E-W-trending fault lies about 2-2.5 km north of the depression; the original authors explicitly identify pockmark origin as an alternative requiring investigation.
Official Indian exploration summary identifies SR-004 as seabed mapping/morphometry/sediment study off Cochin, Kerala and SR-007 as morphotectonic and sediment-characteristic studies of Laxmi Ridge.
observed_target_evidence.source: Indian Bureau of Mines / Indian Minerals Yearbook exploration summary

fluid_escape.geometry: approximately 900 x 450 m wide, 22 m deep, in approximately 155 m water depth
diagnostics: gas-related bright reflectors reported near top of chimney

fluid_escape.reported_context: Published western Indian margin pockmarks occur in 145-330 m water depth; migration of biogenic/thermogenic gas or pore fluids along faults is a proposed origin.
fluid_escape.source_context: Dandapath et al. 2010 as summarized in the SR-004 publication

diagnostics: shocked quartz identified in 12 drill-core samples
normal and reverse faults associated with crater structure
shocked minerals adjacent to crater floor

current_hypothesis_ranking.reason: SR-004 scale is compatible with known large pockmarks; fault proximity and truncated subsurface geometry are compatible with fluid migration/collapse. The original size-based argument against pockmarks is not decisive given modern giant-pockmark controls.
Circular isolated morphology plus reported magnetic/gravity behavior keep impact live, but no diagnostic shock metamorphism, impact breccia or impact melt has yet been demonstrated.
Nearby faulting may provide a structural explanation independent of active seepage.
No currently available observation requires or supports an artificial origin.

fluid_escape_support: vertical seismic chimney/pipe beneath the depression
acoustic blanking or gas-related bright spots
methane-derived authigenic carbonate or seep-related mineralization
impact_support: central uplift or excavation geometry compatible with crater mechanics

killer_test.test: Acquire multichannel seismic or highest-resolution SBP through the exact center of SR-004 and co-register it with MBES, magnetic and gravity profiles.
killer_test.impact_favoring_result: excavation/damage architecture, crater fill and impact-style deformation without a feeder chimney, ideally followed by diagnostic shock mineralogy
killer_test.fluid_escape_favoring_result: vertical chimney/pipe, acoustic blanking/bright spots, fault-fed geometry and seep geochemistry

next_data_targets: exact official SR-004 depression center coordinates
full-resolution SBP line crossing the depression
metadata and exact coordinates for the 12.5 m central core
core sedimentology/mineralogy/geochemistry beyond the coarse-fraction shock screen
later GSI cruises or repeat surveys intersecting the feature

epistemic_firewall.age: UNKNOWN; Holocene age inference in the 2016 paper is not a direct event date
